items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He and I worked at this fruit sugar-coating factory which was at least 6 miles from where we lived.

ctx.x: Dad, my brother and I moved from 9th Street to Hathaway Street and I went to work in a fruit sugar-coating factory. There was a family living on the first floor by the name of Haddins that were distant cousins of ours. One of the Haddins had married the daughter of my Aunt Mary. On the second floor was a family named Huston. We had two rooms and a kitchen on the third floor and there was a man that lived in a small room on the side of our front room.

The Huston's were from way down South and their son came to Cincinnati to live with them after we had been living on Hathaway Street a few months. This fellow was older than I and he loved to carry a pistol. He and I worked at this fruit sugar-coating factory which was at least 6 miles from where we lived. We rode the street car to work and walked home when the work day was finished. My sister stayed with us sometimes and with my mother at times.

My father was offered a job by a rich family near Lexington, Ky., as a cook and he accepted. He rented our apartment to a man named Wade and took my brother to Kentucky with him. My sister went back to stay with my mother and I was allowed to stay with the Wade family which consisted of Mr. Wade, his mother and his son. My father allowed me to stay because I was working, but he told me that if anything went wrong, I should come back to Kentucky.
